messages:
maria: Quick sync — while running load tests we saw a flurry of read-repair work during cold warmups for small tenants. Putting notes here and proposing a lightweight playbook to avoid noisy repair storms.

jason: Ugh, saw that too. 10s of repair RPCs for a single hotspot when a node reboots.

sam: Can you paste a small trace? would help root-cause.

maria: Paste of a condensed trace: ```
[2026-03-20T13:02:11Z] get(prefix=A123) -> miss -> fetch-> populate -> success
[2026-03-20T13:02:11Z] read-repair(probe) triggered for A123 -> parallel repair RPCs x4
[2026-03-20T13:02:12Z] repair backfill writes -> eviction churn -> more misses
```

lee: Two quick hypotheses: (1) warmup policy eagerly triggers probe repairs for every miss until residency epoch settles; (2) observer sidecar isn't suppressing duplicate prefill requests.

carla: Related: we saw the same pattern when the prefix lease bounced during upgrade. repair + prefill doubled traffic.

maria: Proposed playbook (short):
1) During node warmup, apply a "soft-warm" window (T_warm = 30s) where:
   - prefill requests are rate-limited per-prefix (token-bucket 10req/s).
   - read-repair becomes probabilistic: only 1/4th of misses trigger a full repair probe.
2) Add a short-circuit: if a prefix already has an in-flight prefill in the last 100ms, coalesce.
3) Emit metrics: prefills_coalesced, readrepair_suppressed, warm_miss_ratio.
4) Migration rollout: enable soft-warm for a small fleet % then increase after observing metrics for 48h.

jason: That seems reasonable. The probabilistic repair is safe as long as client-visible consistency is within SLA. We should document the degradation tradeoff — stale reads versus load.

sam: Implementation notes: we can reuse the existing prefill-token-bucket code and a small in-memory coalescer keyed by prefix+epoch. Coalescer TTL 100ms.

lee: Config sketch (ini-style):
```
[warmup]
T_warm_ms=30000
prefill_rate_per_prefix=10
readrepair_prob_numerator=1
readrepair_prob_denominator=4
coalesce_ttl_ms=100
```

carla: Also add a deploy-time safety flag so we can immediately disable probabilistic repair if anomalies show up. Something like `repair_mode=probabilistic|always|off`.

maria: Agreed. Also propose a test plan:
- unit: coalescer correctness + race tests (simulated concurrent prefill triggers)
- integration: chaos test where node is restarted, assert repair RPCs drop by >= 60% during warm window
- canary: 5% fleet, 24h telemetry review (prefills_coalesced, client_error_rate, tail-latency)

jason: One more edge: long-lived cursors that resume during warm window might rely on immediate repair. We should add an override: cursor-resume requests set a header `x-repair-priority:high` to bypass probabilistic suppression.

sam: Good call. We'll need to validate that bypass with canary users only.

carla: Who owns the rollout tasks? I'd volunteer to own telemetry dashboards + alert thresholds.

maria: Thanks. I'll own the config + code changes PR. Sam/Lee can pair on unit/integration tests. Jason will review the consistency trade doc.

deploy-bot: Deploy ticket created: https://tickets.internal/INF-9142 assigned to maria, carla, sam; canary tag added. :white_check_mark:

lee: Minor: add a debug flag to force-repair-probability=0/1 for in-situ debugging.

maria: Added to TODO. Action items summarized:
- maria: draft PR with config + coalescer implementation (ETA 3d)
- carla: telemetry + dashboard (ETA 2d)
- sam/lee: tests + chaos scenario (ETA 5d)
- jason: write up short consistency tradeoff doc (ETA 1d)

jason: Also capturing decision: default is `repair_mode=probabilistic` during warmup window only. Permanent behavior unchanged.

maria: Thanks all — will follow up in PR with links. If anyone sees a blocker in tests call me or @maria directly. :slightly_smiling_face:
